title: 2 Chronicles 30
paragraphs: ¹ Hezekiah sent word to all of Israel and Judah, and wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh as well, inviting everyone to come to the house of the LORD in Jerusalem and celebrate the Passover in honor of the LORD, the God of Israel. ² The king had consulted with his officials and the whole assembly in Jerusalem, and they agreed to keep the Passover in the second month — ³ because the priests had not yet consecrated themselves in sufficient numbers, and the people had not yet gathered in Jerusalem to make it possible to do it at the appointed time. ⁴ The decision pleased the king and the whole assembly. ⁵ So they issued a decree to send a proclamation throughout all Israel, from Beersheba to Dan, calling people to come to Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the LORD, the God of Israel — for it had not been observed as the law prescribed for a very long time.

⁶ The royal couriers set out with letters from the king and his officials, traveling through all of Israel and Judah, carrying this message from the king: "People of Israel, return to the LORD, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to those of you who remain — those who escaped the hand of the kings of Assyria. ⁷ Do not be like your ancestors and your fellow Israelites who were unfaithful to the LORD, the God of their fathers — you can see what became of them: he handed them over to destruction. ⁸ Do not be stubborn now as they were. Submit yourselves to the LORD and come to his sanctuary, which he has consecrated forever. Serve the LORD your God, and his fierce anger will turn away from you. ⁹ If you return to the LORD, your relatives and children will be shown mercy by those who hold them captive, and they will come back to this land — for the LORD your God is gracious and compassionate; he will not turn his face from you if you return to him." ¹⁰ The couriers traveled from city to city through Ephraim and Manasseh, all the way to Zebulun — but the people laughed at them and mocked them.

¹¹ Nevertheless, some from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem. ¹² In Judah, too, God moved the people to act with one heart, carrying out the command of the king and his officials as directed by the word of the LORD. ¹³ A very large assembly gathered in Jerusalem to keep the Festival of Unleavened Bread in the second month. ¹⁴ They set to work removing the pagan altars in Jerusalem, and all the incense altars they took down and threw into the Kidron Valley. ¹⁵ On the fourteenth day of the second month, they slaughtered the Passover lamb. The priests and Levites were moved by shame to consecrate themselves and bring the burnt offerings to the house of the LORD.

¹⁶ The priests and Levites stood at their posts in the order prescribed by the law of Moses, the man of God. The priests sprinkled the blood that the Levites handed to them. ¹⁷ Since many in the assembly had not consecrated themselves, the Levites were responsible for slaughtering the Passover lambs for all who were not ceremonially clean, to consecrate the offerings to the LORD. ¹⁸ A large number of the people — many from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun — had not purified themselves, yet they ate the Passover contrary to what was written. But Hezekiah prayed for them, saying, "May the good LORD pardon ¹⁹ everyone who sets their heart on seeking God — the LORD, the God of their ancestors — even if they have not been cleansed according to the purification rites of the sanctuary." ²⁰ And the LORD heard Hezekiah and healed the people.

²¹ The Israelites who were present in Jerusalem kept the Festival of Unleavened Bread for seven days with tremendous joy. The Levites and priests praised the LORD day after day, accompanied by resounding instruments of music. ²² Hezekiah spoke encouragingly to all the Levites who showed such skill in serving the LORD. They ate the festival food for the full seven days, offering fellowship offerings and giving thanks to the LORD, the God of their ancestors. ²³ Then the entire assembly decided to keep the festival for another seven days, and they did so with great joy. ²⁴ Hezekiah king of Judah had contributed a thousand bulls and seven thousand sheep to the assembly, and the officials had given them a thousand bulls and ten thousand sheep. A large number of priests also consecrated themselves. ²⁵ The whole assembly of Judah rejoiced — the priests, the Levites, all who had come from Israel, the foreigners who lived in Israel, and those who dwelt in Judah.

²⁶ There was great joy in Jerusalem, for nothing like this had been seen since the days of Solomon son of David, king of Israel. ²⁷ Then the priests and the Levites rose and blessed the people, and their voices were heard — their prayer rose up to God's holy dwelling place in heaven.
